'''Péter Lévai''' (born 8 August 1962 in [[Miskolc]]) is a Hungarian physicist, research professor, director general of HUN-REN Wigner Fizikai Kutatóközpont<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Wigner Fizikai Kutatóközpont |url=https://tdf.kormany.hu/download/8/0d/71000/Dr%20L%C3%A9vai%20P%C3%A9ter%20prezent%C3%A1ci%C3%B3ja.pdf |access-date=2024-07-17 |website=kormany.hu}}</ref> and a full member of the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lévai, Péter (Magfizika) |url=https://m2.mtmt.hu/api/author/10000357?&&labelLang=hun |access-date=2024-07-17 |website=mtmt.hu}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Peter Levai - CV |url=http://www.rmki.kfki.hu/~plevai/currieng.html |access-date=2024-07-17 |website=www.rmki.kfki.hu}}</ref>

== Education ==
Péter Lévai was born in 1962 in [[Miskolc]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Személyi névtér – Nemzeti Névtér |url=https://magyarnemzetinevter.hu/szemelyi-nevter/ |access-date=2024-07-17 |language=hu-HU}}</ref> He graduated in physics from [[Eötvös Loránd University]] in 1986 and was a PhD fellow at the MTA Központi Fizikai Kutatóintézet.<ref name=":1" /> He received his PhD in 1989 and was a research fellow at Institute for Particle and Nuclear Physics of MTA KFKI, and between 1990 and 1992 he was a research fellow at [[Duke University]] and [[Texas A&M University]] in the USA. He has taught [[high-energy nuclear physics]] at ELTE since 1989 and was awarded a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in physics in 1992.<ref name="Köztestületi tagok">{{Cite web |title=Köztestületi tagok |url=https://mta.hu/koztestuleti_tagok |access-date=2024-07-17 |website=mta.hu |language=hu}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Lévai Péter - ODT Személyi adatlap |url=https://doktori.hu/index.php?menuid=192&lang=HU&sz_ID=1848 |access-date=2024-07-17 |website=doktori.hu |language=hu}}</ref>

== Academic career ==
From 1994, he was a senior research fellow at MTA KFKI RMKI, and from 1999 to 2010 he was a scientific advisor.<ref name=":1" />

In 1999 he was awarded a doctorate by the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, and in 2000 he habilitated and became a private lecturer at ELTE.<ref name=":1" />

From 2005 to 2012, he was the leader of the Hungarian ALICE group in the high-energy experiment at [[CERN|European Organization for Nuclear Research]].<ref name=":1" /> From 2010 to 2011, he was deputy director of the MTA KFKI, and in 2011 he became research professor.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Peter LEVAI CV |url=https://wigner.hu/levaipeter |access-date=2026-02-25 |website=wigner.hu}}</ref> Since 2012, he has been Director General of the HUN-REN Wigner Research Centre for Physics.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":0" /><ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Lévai Péter |url=https://mindentudas.hu/szem%C3%A9lyek/8544-levai-peter-21386718.html |access-date=2024-07-17 |website=mindentudas.hu}}</ref> In 2010, he was elected a Corresponding Member of the MTA, and in 2016, he was elected a Full Member.<ref name="Köztestületi tagok"/>

He specializes in [[nuclear physics]], with research interests in the theoretical and experimental study of the strong interaction between elementary particles and the properties of strongly interacting matter, as well as heavy ion collisions.<ref name=":3" />

He is a member of the [[European Academy of Sciences and Arts]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Members |url=https://members.euro-acad.eu/#memberList |access-date=2025-07-17 |website=members.euro-acad.eu}}</ref> and the [[Academia Europaea]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Academy of Europe: Lévai Péter |url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/L%C3%A9vai_P%C3%A9ter |access-date=2025-07-17 |website=www.ae-info.org}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
He is married and has one daughter.<ref name=":1" />
